draft.title: Conditional probability
card: P(A | B) is the probability of A given that B has happened. Knowing B has happened shrinks the sample space to just the outcomes in B.
Formula: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B)/P(B). The bottom is the event we are given. The top is the part of it that is also A.
From a table, P(A | B) = (number in both A and B) ÷ (number in B). Use only the row or column for B as the total.
Example: in a class of 30, 12 play netball, and 8 of those 12 also play tennis. P(tennis | netball) = 8/12 = 2/3. The total is 12, not 30.
draft.remember: Given B means B is the new total. Divide by P(B), not by everything.

a.q: In a group, P(A ∩ B) = 0.2 and P(B) = 0.5. What is P(A | B)?
a.why: P(A | B) = P(A ∩ B) ÷ P(B) = 0.2 ÷ 0.5 = 0.4. Multiplying gives 0.1, but the formula divides by the probability of the given event.
a.clue: The event after the bar goes on the bottom.

b.q: Of 40 students at a school camp, 25 chose kayaking and 10 of those also chose archery. 5 chose only archery. A student who chose archery is picked. What is the probability they also chose kayaking?
b.why: Archery has 10 + 5 = 15 students, and 10 of them chose kayaking, so the probability is 10/15 = 2/3. The option 1/4 divides by all 40 students, which ignores that we are told the student chose archery.
b.clue: Find the total number who chose archery first.

problems.detail: Two options, 2/5 and 10/25, are the same value. A student can rule both out because they cannot both be the single right answer, which weakens the question. Replace one with a different distractor, such as 10/30 or 15/40.

check.summary: The facts and both answers are correct (0.4 and 2/3). In question b, two options (2/5 and 10/25) have the same value, so a student can rule both out by elimination; one should be replaced.
